title: What is truth, again (John 18:33–38)
hook: my kingdom is not of this world

segments.voice: Yesterday, the garden, and the soldiers falling back at two words. Your line was I am he. Did you own something first today? Day five hundred twenty-seven.

Early in the morning, John says, the accusers bring Jesus to the governor's palace, and then stop at the door. It's the Passover, and they won't go in, so they won't be defiled before the feast. So Pilate has to keep crossing the threshold: out to the crowd, in to the prisoner, out again. John builds the whole trial that way, scene by scene, outside and inside. We met Pilate's famous question early on the path. Today we stay inside the room, a prisoner and a governor alone, with the sentence that started it.
screen: `THE ACCUSERS STOP AT THE DOOR.` → `PILATE GOES IN AND OUT.` → `A PRISONER AND A GOVERNOR.`

segments.voice: Pilate asks: art thou the king of the Jews? For Rome, that's the only question. A king is a rival to Caesar. Jesus answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "My kingdom is not of this world." It's easy to hear that as, my kingdom is somewhere else, far away, nothing to do with here. But the Greek says ek tou kosmou, out of this world, from it. He's talking about where his kingdom comes from, not where it isn't. It doesn't grow out of armies and taxes and fear. And he proves it on the spot: if it were that kind of kingdom, he says, his servants would be fighting. A few hours ago, Peter tried, and Jesus told him to put the sword away. Pilate grabs the word: so you are a king? And Jesus says, "For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth. Every one that is of the truth, heareth my voice." Notice what kind of king this is. Not one who commands by force, but one whose people are the ones who hear his voice. That's the good shepherd again, sheep who know the voice. Then Pilate's question, what is truth, and he walks back out to the crowd without waiting for an answer. Look at the two men. One keeps crossing a doorway, trying to satisfy the people outside and Caesar far away. The other stands still. That's the edge of today. A kingdom not from this world isn't a kingdom with nothing to say to this world. It means a loyalty that no flag, party or boss handed out, so none of them gets the whole person.
screen: `ART THOU A KING?` · `NOT OF: NOT FROM THIS WORLD.` · `HIS PEOPLE HEAR HIS VOICE.` · `NO FLAG GETS THE WHOLE PERSON.` · then, large: `WHAT IS TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: ask where your loyalty lies. Sit, and breathe. Let the things that pull on you come to mind one at a time: your job, your phone, a team, a party, a person you want to please, your own reputation. Notice which ones get the most of you, honestly, not ideally. You don't have to rearrange anything. Just see the list. If you pray, you can hold Jesus's words, every one that is of the truth heareth my voice, and listen. If you don't, simply sit with the list. The bell holds the time.
What is truth. Pilate's question to a prisoner who had just said his kingdom is not from this world, and who came to testify to the truth. Today's word.
Your line: not of this world. Today, when something demands all of you, a screen, a fight, a boss, remember it doesn't get the whole person. Day five hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Catholics hear this exchange every Good Friday, when the Passion according to John is read or sung, often with several voices taking the parts of the narrator, Jesus, Pilate and the crowd.

myth: not of this world means his kingdom has nothing to do with here
the Greek means not from this world: its source, not its location.
the accusers went inside to face Jesus with Pilate
they stayed outside for the Passover; Pilate went back and forth.
Jesus says he was born to testify to the truth
for this was I born, and for this came I into the world.

fork.setup: you're on trial before a Roman governor, who asks if you're a king. a yes could mean death. what do you say?
options: my kingdom is not of this world.
fork.reveal: Jesus neither denies it nor claims Caesar's kind of power: my kingdom is not of this world. if it were, his servants would fight.

original.note: Greek: truth, the word in Pilate's question (John 18:38).

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus's kingdom is somewhere far away.
what it means: his kingdom doesn't come from force or fear, and its people are those who hear his voice.
what a scholar hears: ek tou kosmou marks origin, not location; John stages the trial in alternating scenes, outside with the crowd and inside with Jesus.

notes: Revisits Pilate (year 1, day 63 covered 'what is truth', the hand washing and the Latin anagram); this day focuses on 'not of this world'.
John 18:28 (accusers stay outside so as not to be defiled before the Passover) paraphrased; the outside/inside alternation of the trial scenes is a common reading of John 18:28–19:16. Confirm.
Good Friday Passion is John 18:1–19:42, often read in parts. Confirm.
